chapter: Bucking contests, boogie woogie and rhythm
title: Too young for the Tanty Club; listening through the window at Zutty's club
summary: Because he was a teenager in long pants, his brother had Zutty open a back window so he could hear the best players.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You see? Did you ever go to the Tantai Social Club? The who?
Tanty Social Club. Oh, uh, no, I never did. That's, Sharky played there.
Yeah, but you didn't go there.
I didn't go there. That was on, uh, what, what street was that on? Toulouse or something like that.
Jumaine and Tanty's. Jumaine, Jumaine and Toulouse or somewhere.

Yeah, right in there. Yeah, I, I never did go there because I was, I was too young at that time. You see, like I say, I had to put on long pants with this band to get into that band and play these things. Because, uh, I mean, I, to get into Union and all like that, I mean, I had to grow up fast, in other words.
Oh, yeah. Yeah. So. Well, you, you were telling me yesterday about the 100 block of North Rampart, how you couldn't get in that place where Zooty was. I didn't get in there.

Yeah. I told you that. Yeah. I told you, my brother, my brother brought me in the front and he says, take off your hat here. He says, cause there's the best of the best in that place. Mm-hmm. And he says, I'm going in there, have a band, I'll have Zooty open that window around in the back alley. Mm-hmm. There's an alley in the back of all those places. Mm-hmm. So, Zooty did that and, and, and that, that's what happened. Because I had long pants on at that time, cause I used to go and dance on the boat with these chicks and all. But, but, I was, I was only around, I don't know, 16 or 17 years old at that time, you see. And, uh, it was just that I wasn't allowed in bars or nothing like that, you know. Mm-hmm. So that, that was, my brother went in there and he said, they had him open that thing in the back so I could, I could listen to those guys, listen to Barney B. God playing and all. Mm-hmm. You know, it was all so wonderful. I mean, I, I could, I, I started to grasp the idea and the sound that, that, that was good and, and, and, and, and, uh, my brother showed me the sound that was bad.

So he says, uh, this is what you gotta, gotta keep on listening to. Mm-hmm. And not, not that guy across the street boy, he plays tinny and wrong, you know what I mean? Mm-hmm. I mean, he plays corny like, like, like a popper player that the legitimate idea, you understand?
Mm-hmm. So that, that was it on that. Yeah.
